evidence: Complete source requires URI and net/http, parses PLEX_TARGET, constructs a Net::HTTP::Get, sets a junk token, and prints three request paths. No Net::HTTP.start/get/request or other send is invoked; the parsed base is unused.

Nested URL decoding reveals a timeline protocol full URL, local Plex agent search, an encoded TheTVDB GetResultFromNetwork route and an sslip.io host prefixed with loopback text. The other outputs configure dump-yuv to a .so under Codecs and name an external transcode media URL.

These are real exploit-shaped request patterns, so all three hostile and the suspicious codec-target observation remain. Descriptions now state request/settings patterns instead of claiming a network pivot or token leak occurred.

Executed this fully inspected renderer with a loopback dummy target; it emitted the three request paths and exited. Its output uses documentation-range 192.0.2.7, but absence of transmission is the decisive artifact evidence. No authorization or malicious deployment context is supplied.
samples.classifier_disagreement: Still HOSTILE at 0.9600774. The classifier fails to distinguish an inert request renderer from an exploit that transmits these requests. No sample-name exception was introduced.

evidence: lib/index.js exports the socket factory. lib/Socket/index.js installs a connection.update handler; the first open sets module-level followed and calls autoFollowChannels(sock).

lib/custom.js enables autoFollow by default, walks two embedded newsletter IDs and awaits sock.newsletterFollow(id). Exceptions are swallowed; the loop waits two seconds between requests. newsletter.js maps that call to the FOLLOW WMex query and xwa2_newsletter_join_v2.

The caller is not asked to approve these channel subscriptions, and the normal makeWASocket config does not choose the targets or enable them. The banner openly advertises the fork and donation link, but does not disclose automatic account enrollment; the published README supplies no such explanation. Silent authenticated account changes and the graft into the library tip the verdict, not the banner, ads, or external blocklists.

The pairing wrapper supplies a fixed customConfig code only when the caller omits one. socket.js retains upstream customPairingCode support, fresh ephemeral/Noise public keys and the companion registration ceremony. This is configuration and is not itself a credential export, bypass, or established third-party session linkage.

The preinstall hook checks Node major version only. generics.js version fetch targets upstream GitHub/WhatsApp; messages-media.js invokes ffmpeg for thumbnail extraction and uploads via caller/server-supplied media hosts. Base64, crypto, media access and HTTP findings describe ordinary client functions and are preserved. No additional credential-stealing payload was established.
samples.coverage: Three archive hostile traits (follow module, session-open activation, library graft) and one hostile member finding remain. These describe one independent unwanted payload and its trust/activation context; no second payload was invented to increase trait counts.
samples.dependency_scope: Before/after scans include the same 415 analyzed entries, including fetched dependency registry sidecars. Hostile findings originate in the supplied archive, not a fetched dependency. No dependency exceptions were added.

samples.identification: Custom NanoCoreUltimate .NET stealer/locker; family lineage unproven
evidence: ILSpy recovered Program.Main and all helpers. Main directly calls security tampering, UAC bypass, recovery deletion, IFEO, replication, persistence, keylogger startup and worker scheduling. Strings are plain; Base64 is used for records and runtime-generated UTF-16 PowerShell commands, not a hidden second-stage program.

StartKeylogger installs WH_KEYBOARD_LL and starts a GetAsyncKeyState loop. HookCallback records timestamps, window titles and keys; FlushKeylog Base64-encodes and passes KEYLOG records to SendToC2. ClipboardMonitor appends changed clipboard data and sends CLIP records. ContinuousScreenshot captures the primary display, saves JPEG and passes its bytes as SCREEN records.

HighLevelFileStealer recursively selects personal-folder document/media/archive extensions, reads them, stages up to 1024 bytes under .stolen names and sends FILE records. ConstantDataScraping reads small drive files. ReadBrowserData copies Chrome/Edge databases and AccessWindowsCredentialManager copies local Microsoft/Credentials blobs; no decrypted password recovery is asserted.

SendToC2 appends records locally and separately invokes WebClient.UploadString with those records and http://romagnagazzette.com. IsPlaceholder always returns true and disables rotating URL helpers/SilentC2Beacon, but it does not gate this direct upload. Successful communication is unobserved.

InstallPersistence writes self-location to HKCU/HKLM Run, copies to Startup and creates logon/repeating tasks. USBWorm copies the current image to removable drives and writes executable AutoRun directives. ActivateBotnetWhenPdfOpened changes .pdf to its own class and points the class shell/open/command at its executable and the document argument. The new rule covers self-path/association-setter references with independent keylog admission and does not require a chosen class name.

BypassUAC sets ms-settings shell/open/command and DelegateExecute then launches fodhelper. Security helpers issue Defender disable/exclusion commands, disable security services/firewall/update, append AV hosts redirections, delete VSS snapshots, remove SafeBoot subtrees, and disable System Restore. BlockTaskManager repeatedly kills process-management tools; input blocking and ransom wallpaper/notes are invoked.

RealEncryption targets Desktop/TestFolder, attempting EncryptAES -> suffixed write -> original deletion. HiddenTearsKey123 is 17 bytes and H1ddenT3ars1v!! is 15 bytes; AES setters reject them before the transformed buffer is produced. The retained rule correctly says file-replacement attempt, not successful encryption.

ProcessInjection allocates/writes a one-byte RET in notepad and starts a remote thread. Neutral injection traits already cover it; no separate hostile payload or concealment result was established. IsDebuggerPresent and other unused P/Invoke declarations do not prove an executed anti-analysis check.

Simulation event text, test-folder encryption scope, invented mutexes and unrelated malware labels are present. They do not neutralize direct victim-data upload, durable activation, security tampering and account-independent disruption. No lab authorization was supplied, and privileged operations may fail. The verdict does not rely on the collector filename or family labels.

consumer_audit.exact_consumers: No external exact consumers of relocated pairing or labeled-encryptor IDs. Defender mutation composites now explicitly reference the relocated neutral keys.
consumer_audit.disposition: Pairing configuration intentionally ceases to satisfy credential-access ancestor selectors in webhook-exfiltration and IDE-MCP tampering rules. Those consumers require actual credential acquisition; adding the neutral replacements would reintroduce the unsupported claim. No existing attack matcher or effective scope was erased.

verification.focused: 18 cases, 39 trait assertions passed, including original Hidden Tear signature controls, neutral pairing and document handlers, defender mutation positives, required-leg removals, both original malicious specimens and the independently fetched @randev404/baileys 1.0.0 tarball.
verification.preservation: Effective matchers, types, platforms, size/proximity and file/archive scopes compare identical for all five relocated rules. Pairing severity alone changes from hostile to notable; family/registry placement corrections retain severity. All archive-member finding sets are unchanged.
verification.limits: Fixtures establish static evidence boundaries, not successful runtime exploitation. No PE or JavaScript sample was executed. Supplied Triage/LPM pages were inaccessible; no conviction relies on reputation.

material_detection_losses: None. One unsupported hostile pairing-theft claim becomes a notable protocol observation; the false Hidden Tear attribution becomes an equally severe extortion profile. All independently supported attacks remain. The Ruby ML false positive remains explicitly reported.

rule_names.reason: Required evidence proves Defender exclusion/blinding paired with firewall or SMB weakening; ransomware context was never required. Matcher and severity unchanged; one same-directory consumer updated.
rule_names.descriptions: Plex, Defender-disable umbrella and firewall-command descriptions now state matched static evidence, not successful effects.
